name: crime_type_names
description: The crime type name load of 7 (CQ8). (1) Values [1] and [2] of 0x8A416B2E are the LTEXT group G and instance I; value [0] is ignored and the LTEXT type is always 0x2026960B: type 0x50 names its key with type 0x12345678 and still gets the text of (0x2026960B, G, I). (2) The host looks up (0x2026960B, G + language ID, I), then (0x2026960B, G, I) (data-formats 6.2; the plugin's part, this host's table holds what that lookup finds). (3) The text is copied and detokenized; (4) every U+2022 becomes U+200B (data-formats 6.1): 0x51's 'A•B•' loads as 'A​B​'. If the load fails, the inline string 0xAA12FCB0 replaces the name when present (0x52: no such LTEXT -> 'Inline'; 0x53: the detokenizer returned false -> 'Inline'); otherwise the name is empty: a failed load leaves it empty in every case (CQ16), the text a failed detokenizer left included (0x54: '#who#•' is discarded -> ''), and with no LTEXT (0x55 -> ''). [choice] (CQ17) A key with fewer than 3 values, or a scalar, is missing: no lookup (0x56 -> 'Inline'; 0x58, a scalar with no 0xAA12FCB0 -> ''). The inline string is read only when the load fails (0x57 has both: the LTEXT wins). Hand-derived from the four steps.
